rootNote: Teaching root chosen from WLC counts (OSHB 3d15126): H5066 נָגַשׁ has 125 verb tokens in 5 stems (Qal 68, Hiphil 37, Niphal 17, Hophal 2, Hitpael 1), the most stems of any frequent I-Nun root that has Qal and no second weakness. It is also the paradigm root of GKC §66 / Paradigm H and Davidson §33. Its Qal perfect is not used in the Bible (the Niphal perfect serves), so those squares take examples from other I-Nun roots. Example words for squares the root lacks come from other I-Nun roots with no second weakness.
source: Forms from GKC §66 + Paradigm H (Verbs פ״ן) and Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar §33 paradigm (p. 168), both in /workspace/hebrew-books/. Squares those tables call 'regular' (Qal perfect, Piel, Pual, Hitpael, and person forms the tables omit) follow GKC §66.2 ('The other forms are all quite regular') applied to the strong-verb.json pattern; each cell's formBasis says which ('book' = printed in GKC or Davidson; 'rule' = regular pattern per GKC §66.2). Not copied from any copyrighted chart. Where K&J (the BBH stand-in) prints a square we had built by rule, the K&J form is used with formBasis 'printed'; K&J's -ָה feminine participles are 'printed' alternates (tutor rulings 2026-11-21 4:09 PM ET; see tools/kj_rulings.py).
verificationMethod: Each form was matched (consonants + vowel points, accents ignored, dagesh lene and plene/defective holam, shureq and ḥireq-yod spellings normalized) against OSHB morphhb-wlc tokens with the same OSHB morph slot. Radical slots are R1 נ, R2 ג, R3 שׁ; where the root nun is assimilated it is not written and is taken as נ. The example's root (with shin/sin dot) was checked against the Strong's headword for its lemma number. Example roots must be I-Nun with no second weakness (2nd radical not guttural/ר/ו/י; 3rd not guttural/ר/ה/ו/י/נ; not geminate); נָתַן is excluded. H5266 and H5400 are excluded per GKC §66 (אֶסַּק Ps 139:8 from סלק; נִשְּׂקָה Ps 78:21 from שׂלק). Ketiv tokens are excluded. Imperatives may carry paragogic ה (OSHB Sh); infinitives construct may carry a preposition (examplePrefix). Example preference: teaching root (no prefix, then ו, then preposition), then another I-Nun root in the same order. Every matched token was cross-checked against STEPBible TAHOT (see tahot field and VERIFY-weak-inun.md).

notes.cohortative: Cohortative = 1st-person yiqtol + ָה: Qal אֶגְּשָׁה (Davidson p.168), Hiphil אַגִּישָׁה (Davidson p.168). Shown as a note, not a table row.
notes.jussive: As in the strong verb, the jussive looks like yiqtol except in Hiphil (יַגֵּשׁ vs יַגִּישׁ).
notes.weqatal: Qal vav-consecutive perfect וְנָגַשְׁתָּ (Davidson p.168). Shown as a note, not a column.
notes.qalOType: Qal has two I-Nun types (GKC §66.1(a)-(b); Paradigm H). נגשׁ is the a-imperfect type (יִגַּשׁ, imperative גַּשׁ, infinitive גֶּשֶׁת). The o-imperfect type keeps the nun in imperative and infinitive: נָפַל, יִפֹּל, imperative נְפֹל, infinitive נְפֹל. נָתַן is special (final nun also assimilates; imperfect יִתֵּן, imperative תֵּן, infinitive תֵּת; GKC §66 Rem. 3) and is not used as an example in this table.
notes.assimilation: Rule: a nun that closes a syllable assimilates into the next consonant, which then carries dagesh forte (GKC §66.2; Davidson §33). This happens in Qal yiqtol/wayyiqtol, Niphal qatal and participle, all Hiphil and all Hophal. It does not happen where the nun has its own vowel: Qal qatal/participles/infinitive absolute, Niphal yiqtol/imperative/infinitives, Piel, Pual, Hitpael.
notes.secondGuttural: If the 2nd radical is a guttural, the nun usually stays (יִנְחַל; GKC §66 Rem. 1). Such roots are not used as examples here.
notes.Hophal imperative: None: GKC Paradigm H and Davidson p.168 both mark it 'wanting'.
